I want a rectangular box that is 220mm wide, 300mm long and 160mm high. Let it be on the upside open and have walls with 8mm thickness and a 12mm thick bottom. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step implementation strategy (no execution yet)

1. Establish the outer shell  
   • Create one additive block that defines the external dimensions of the box:  
     – x-size 220 mm, y-size 300 mm, z-size 160 mm.  
     – Basepoint (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0).  
     – subtraction = False (this block starts the volume).

2. Hollow out the inside to form the cavity and the open top  
   • Create a second block that will be subtracted from the first:  
     – Wall thickness = 8 mm on all vertical faces, so inner width = 220 − 2·8 = 204 mm and inner length = 300 − 2·8 = 284 mm.  
     – Bottom thickness = 12 mm, so the inner cavity starts 12 mm above the base; its height = 160 − 12 = 148 mm.  
     – Basepoint of this inner block = (8, 8, 12).  
     – subtraction = True (so it removes material, leaving walls and bottom).

3. Finish: no further geometry or forces are required; close with finished(allFunctionsCalled=True) when executing.

When you are ready, ask me to prepare the exact block() and finished() calls.
